text:
Alex Chen: Hey team, I'm scheduling a new on-call shadowing run for anyone joining the rotation next month. Want to lock down primary/secondary overlap and make sure runbook pointers are obvious. :wave:

Maria Lopez: +1. I onboarded Ben last week and noticed the paging playbook link is buried in the runbook index. We should highlight the quick-escalation steps.

Samir Patel: I can do a slot for weekday evenings (PST). Do we have gaps between 03:00-06:00 UTC on weekends? I think that's where we had no secondary last month.

Jen Huang: We do have a gap Saturday 04:00-06:00 UTC (that's early PST). I can swap one weekend if someone can cover an evening in return.

Priya Rao: I'm happy to cover that Saturday morning gap once during the month. Also let's make the shadow checklist explicit: what the shadow does during an active page, who speaks to customers, and when to escalate to SRE lead.

Alex Chen: Great. I'll draft a short checklist. Draft idea: 1) Confirm alert details in PagerDuty, 2) Pull recent deploys, 3) Check model-serving metrics (latency > 500ms?), 4) Follow incident runbook.

IncidentBot: [AUTOMATED] New incident template: "pg-serving-latency" available at https://docs.redwood.com/runbooks/pg-serving-latency. Use `/incident start pg-serving-latency` to create an incident channel.

Ben (oncall-shadow): Quick Q — during my shadow I should only observe or can I acknowledge pages? I know we usually have shadows mute pages but want to follow the right protocol.

Maria Lopez: For the first 2 shadows, observe-only (no ack). Then during the final shadow you can acknowledge with coach present. We'll add that to the runbook.

Samir Patel: Can we add a tiny cheat-sheet for triage commands? e.g.:
```
# check node health
kubectl get pods -n serving -l app=redwood-serving
# tail recent logs for model runtime
kubectl logs -n serving svc/model-runtime-0 -c runtime --since=10m
# metric check
curl -s http://metrics.internal/latency?model=all | jq '.p99'
```

Jen Huang: Love the commands. Also add the shortcut to trigger fallback routing: `curl -X POST https://ops.redwood/internal/fallback -d '{"policy":"degrade_to_cpu"}'` — only on approval from primary.

Priya Rao: I'll update the shadow calendar invite to include timezone-aware slots and a pointer to the incident CLI snippet. Also adding a note: if the page hits SEV 2+ and customer is impacted, primary must DM product oncall and ping #customer-impact.

Alex Chen: OK actionable list:
- Maria to surface quick-escalation steps in runbook (due EOD Wed)
- Priya to update calendar & invite with TZ slots (done Thu)
- Samir/Jen to swap weekend if needed (sync in thread)
- Ben to observe first 2 then ack on 3rd shadow (Ben confirmed)

Ben (oncall-shadow): Confirmed. Happy to shadow two weekday evenings and one weekend morning.

Maria Lopez: One more: add a tiny decision tree in runbook for customer-visible incidents:
- Is customer-facing latency degraded? -> Yes -> start incident, set severity 2, notify product, enable fallback routing.
- Is internal queue growth only? -> No immediate customer notice, escalate to runtime team.

Alex Chen: I'll put up a short PR to the runbook and ping the team when it's live. If anyone cannot make their scheduled shadow, please post here so we can swap. Thanks! :thumbsup:

IncidentBot: [REMINDER] On-call handbook quick read requested for new shadows: https://docs.redwood.com/oncall/quick-read (expected 30m).

Samir Patel: noted, I'll read it before my first shadow.

Jen Huang: Thanks everyone. I'll mark the weekend slot covered with Priya.

Priya Rao: Done — calendar invite updated and includes runbook links + triage snippet.

Alex Chen: Closing the loop: I'll merge the runbook PR after Maria's edits and then set a small onboarding doc in the sandbox channel for Ben to practice. We'll treat the first real page as a learning exercise only.

Ben (oncall-shadow): Thanks — appreciate the guidance.
